title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: US hits Iran's Qeshm in Hormuz
preheader: Washington calls the strikes defensive as Tehran warns of a wider response.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Tuesday, November 03, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_important: The US carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said. Washington called them defensive measures against Iranians who used surface-to-air missiles against US assets. The strikes come just before US midterms, and Trump says a deal with Iran 'could happen.'
stories.what_overlooked: The Wall Street Journal reported the strikes, and an anonymous US official confirmed them. Washington has not publicly announced them or given a full account.
stories.prediction: Iran's response to the Qeshm strike, or public US confirmation, would show whether both sides are holding back.

stories.story_title: US sets Russia-Ukraine talks for Abu Dhabi on November 10-11
stories.why_important: The US will bring Russian and Ukrainian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11. They will discuss ending the war, post-war security and how to lower tensions. US envoy Steve Witkoff announced the working-level talks, the first such three-way meeting since February.
stories.what_overlooked: The talks involve officials, not a summit, and no ceasefire has been agreed. Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent Washington.
stories.prediction: Whether Moscow sends a senior delegation to Abu Dhabi will show if the Kremlin is serious about talks.

stories.story_title: Cyberattack disables supermarket fridges across Europe
stories.why_important: A cyberattack on Danfoss refrigeration systems hit supermarkets in at least nine European countries. It raised temperatures and forced food to be thrown away, and the EU warned the incident appears deliberate. The same maker's systems also came under attack in France last month.
stories.what_overlooked: The attacks are hitting the same kind of equipment from one company. That suggests attackers are reusing a known method, not carrying out isolated hacks.
stories.prediction: A second wave of hacks could show whether a government is behind this. Danfoss or an EU agency naming the attackers would also show it.

views.framing: Relays US officials’ defensive claim and limited scope, while noting Iranian state media reported explosions.
